correctness.rationale: The upper bound is exactly Seeger's critical specialization at \((d,p,q)=(2,1,2)\). For the lower bound, the exact matching identity is valid even with repeated target atoms: after multiplying an optimal transport plan by \(2N\), the bipartite transportation polytope has integral supplies two at each indexed quantizer slot and unit demands at each indexed target atom, so an integral optimum pairs the targets; triangle inequality gives the reverse matching bound, while placing one quantizer on each matched segment gives equality. The multiscale construction has \(K=\lfloor\log N/(4\log8)\rfloor\), radii \(8^j\), and \(2m_j^2\) grid atoms per scale. Its second moment is at most \(1/8\). Scale separation makes every matching edge incident to a scale-j special point cost at least its local separation in the required edgewise sense, giving total matching cost at least \(\sqrt{NK}/32\) for large N and therefore \(e_N\ge(1/64)\sqrt{K/N}\), which is the claimed \(\sqrt{\log N/N}\) order. The bundled finite verifier checks only representative floor inequalities; the all-N result rests on the analytic estimates.
